manifest.name: dsh-session-notify
manifest.description: Reply and attention toasts for DeepSeek Harness: a dismissible stack that names the workspace and session, previews the reply or the pending question, and opens the session on click.

readme.text:
Reply toasts for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-harness/deepseek-harness) sessions.

Run several sessions in parallel across different workspaces, and the one you are
not looking at still needs your attention. This plugin watches every session on
the Host and, when a background session finishes answering, pushes a
WeChat-style toast into the top center of the Web UI:

- **Title** — `<workspace folder>-<session title>`, one line, ellipsized.
- **Body** — the first characters of the reply, two lines, ellipsized.
- **Attention** — a background session that asks a question or waits for a tool
  approval shows the same card in amber, with the question text; it goes away by
  itself once that session runs again.
- **Stack** — up to six cards, newest on top; older cards stay until you close them.
- **Close** — every card has its own `×` in the top-right corner.
- **Jump** — clicking a card opens that session.
- **Look** — a light card on a wide, soft shadow: 18px radius, top-to-bottom
  gradient, and a top-down fade in and out.
- **Quiet** — the session you are already reading never toasts, and neither do
  internal subagent children.

The package is a DSH bundle: a Host row plus a browser half. Install it into the
running profile from the directory that holds this `package.json`:

```
plugin_manager install_bundle  target: /absolute/path/to/dsh-session-notify
```

Or, from a shell inside the profile:

```sh
pnpm add /absolute/path/to/dsh-session-notify
```

then add `dsh-session-notify` to the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (or enable the
row in the Plugin Manager). Reload the page once: the browser half is served from
the installed package, so a fresh page load is what activates it.

Uninstall with `plugin_manager remove_bundle` (or remove the row).

The browser half reads no Loader row config, so the knobs are constants at the
top of `client.js`. Edit them and reload the page:

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `maxToasts` | `6` | Cards kept on screen; the oldest fall off the bottom. |
| `ttlMs` | `0` | Auto-dismiss delay. `0` keeps a card until it is closed; a positive value pauses while the window is hidden. |
| `pageMessages` | `8` | Message records requested by one tail read. |
| `maxBodyChars` | `200` | Longest reply excerpt kept; CSS owns the visible lines. |
| `includeActiveSession` | `false` | Also toast the session open in this window. |

1. The browser half subscribes to the forwarded `api-session/status` event and
   reacts when a session stops running.
2. It reads that session's projection watermark (`session/projections`), which
   carries the durable title and the effective working directory.
3. It reads one message-aligned history page through `session/page`, ending at
   that watermark, and takes the last assistant message of the page.
4. If that message is the reply that ends the turn, the toast is published into
   the frame-wide `shell.overlay` slot. The session is never opened, so the
   notification costs one short read and does not touch the workspace view.

The attention tone comes from the two forwarded waterfalls that block a turn:
`user-questions/request` and `approval/request`. The plugin reads the asking
session from the listener's scoped context (`ctx.sessions.scopeOf(this)`), shows
the question text, and always calls `next()` so the real answerer still runs.

The plugin keeps no durable state: a page reload starts from an empty stack, and
only replies that finish while the page is open are announced.

The `session` Remote namespace is read with `ctx.get('remote.session')`, not
`ctx.remote.session`: a namespace is mounted on the Client root, while the
`remote.session` property resolves through the calling fiber's associate table
and is undefined from a plugin context.

Built against DeepSeek Harness `0.2.x` (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-*`). It depends on the
shipped browser wire API — the forwarded `api-session/*` events and the
`session.projections` / `session.page` Remote methods — and on the
`shell.overlay` slot. Those are pre-stable: a Harness release that renames one of
them needs a matching plugin release.

The plugin styles itself with the public `--dsw-alias-*` theme tokens and the
`--dsh-frame-overlay-top` inset, so light/dark and the Windows caption are
inherited rather than re-implemented.

```sh
npm test          # node --test: behaviour tests through a fake Client context
node --check client.js
```

The tests load `client.js` the way the page does — through
`window.__ModuleLoader__` — and drive the real event handlers, projection and
page reads, store and card markup. No build step, no dependencies.
